note: L32 domain rubric. Completion needs every domain at 3/4 or better plus all critical practical checks. Scores are self- or mentor-assessed; each met criterion must point at evidence.

criteria.text: Reads process, service, journal and resource evidence before changing anything
Distinguishes a resource bottleneck from a configuration or permission fault
Restores service with the smallest change and proves the correct user/process
Leaves no unrelated process or host change behind
Traces a request hop by hop (DNS, route, port, TLS)
Separates name resolution, connectivity and certificate failures with evidence
Fixes the failing hop without disabling verification or opening extra paths
Explains which direction (ingress/egress) a rule or policy affects
Writes a small, tested Python change with useful exit codes
Handles timeouts, retries and malformed input explicitly
Keeps secrets and customer data out of output and logs
Explains complexity and memory bounds of the code
Reads a plan before applying and names each forcing attribute
Separates configuration, state and the real object
Avoids replacing stateful resources unintentionally
Keeps state local/scoped and versions pinned
Builds a pinned, unprivileged image with a documented entry point
Identifies image identity (ID/digest) and architecture
Proves dependency readiness instead of assuming start order
Removes only labelled lab containers, images and volumes
Uses Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod/Service/EndpointSlice evidence correctly
Distinguishes scheduling, probe, crash and selector failures
Keeps least privilege: auth can-i matrix, no extra bindings, no tokens
Scopes every command to the lab context and namespace
Promotes or deploys an immutable, recorded artifact
Uses release history to say which build serves and why
Performs and verifies a compatible rollback
Knows what a rollback does not undo (data, schema)
Uses metrics, logs and request/trace ids together
States SLI numerator, denominator and exclusions
Alert/SLO rules are tested, not assumed
Keeps label cardinality bounded and dashboards tied to real metric names
Takes and restores a backup into a separate target
Verifies counts AND selected values/checksums
Chooses a recovery point that protects newer data, and says what was lost
Measures the actual recovery interval
Gives a time-stamped, scoped three-minute update
Separates observation, hypothesis and action
Writes a blameless report with owned follow-ups
Defends decisions with rejected alternatives and names remaining gaps
